discovery_layer.scientific_role: Connects donor-cell-engineered EVs with endothelial protection, direct myocardial delivery and PDA/HA-based NiTi surface functionalization.
discovery_layer.evidence_position: Preclinical preparation characterization, cell stress/intervention assays, mouse cardiac-function observations and short-term rat arterial tissue readouts.
citation_contexts: Methods: distinguish particle-based EV dosing, protein-based myocardial delivery and material-associated release.
Discussion: compare engineered EV activity in free, direct-contact and short-term implant settings.

display_title: Engineered cardiac-cell EVs protect endothelium and functionalize NiTi interfaces
summary: EVs from ZFP36-overexpressing AC16 cells improved viability and reduced lipid oxidation in RSL3-stressed endothelial cells. In a separate mouse infarction experiment, direct EV injection improved ventricular function and reduced fibrosis at day 21. A PDA/HA-modified NiTi surface retained and released EV-associated particles. The engineered coating supported endothelial cells in direct contact and improved vascular tissue markers at day 14 in rats.
research_question: Can EVs generated by ZFP36-engineered cardiac cells protect stressed endothelium and contribute biological activity when incorporated into a NiTi vascular interface?
author_summary: The study compares EVs from ZFP36-overexpressing AC16 cells with EVs from empty-vector donor cells. Under RSL3 exposure, engineered EVs improve endothelial viability and mitochondrial membrane-potential readouts and reduce reactive oxygen species and lipid oxidation. A separate mouse MI injection experiment reports higher left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening at day 21, alongside a smaller fibrotic area than with control EVs. A polydopamine/hyaluronic acid coating on NiTi retains 72.80% ± 0.83% of input particles by nanoparticle tracking analysis and releases particles over 14 days in PBS. The direct-contact cell assays compare engineered and control EV coatings. In a three-arm rat arterial-filament experiment, the engineered coating has higher CD31 and α-SMA staining and lower TNF-α, OPN and 4-HNE staining at day 14.

study_profile.study_design: Donor-cell engineering and EV characterization; RSL3-stressed endothelial intervention; intramyocardial EV delivery in mouse MI; PDA/HA NiTi functionalization, particle loading/release and direct-contact assays; rat femoral-artery injury/filament implantation.
study_profile.evidence_type: Preclinical cellular intervention, particle/material characterization, animal cardiac function/histology and arterial tissue-marker measurements.
study_profile.population: AC16 EV-producing cells and HUVEC recipients; male C57BL/6J mice for MI and male Sprague-Dawley rats for arterial injury/implantation.
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Endothelial protective activity of donor-cell-engineered EVs and the resulting NiTi interface under the tested conditions.
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: EV properties, ROS/mitochondrial/lipid oxidation readouts, mouse day-21 cardiac function/fibrosis, particle loading/release, and rat day-14 vascular morphology/markers.

key_findings.claim: Mouse MI measurements supported ZFP36 as a candidate for donor-cell engineering.
key_findings.context: A source-reported transcriptomic nomination followed by a separate day-3 mouse expression comparison.

evidence.label: Mouse model
evidence.value: Male C57BL/6J mice had permanent left anterior descending coronary artery ligation. Sham mice had surgery without ligation. Blood and myocardial tissue were collected on day 3.

evidence.label: Blood qPCR
evidence.value: ZFP36 and ACSL1 higher and GABARAPL1 lower after MI; Figure 1A-C caption n = 5.

evidence.label: Myocardial observations
evidence.value: Higher ZFP36/ACSL1 immunohistochemical positive area and corresponding immunofluorescence; quantitative Figure 1E-F n = 5.

evidence.label: Engineering rationale
evidence.value: Main Results describes screening, mouse expression measurements and prior work on RNA-binding and stress responses as the rationale for selecting ZFP36. It reports that GABARAPL1 changes differed between the human transcriptomic screen and mouse MI, so myocardial staining focused on ZFP36 and ACSL1. Figures S1–S2 contain the discovery details. The precise source cohorts and sample sizes remain unresolved.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF p. 2, Methods §2.2, p. 4, Figure 1A–G and caption, and pp. 5 and 9, Results §3.1. Results cites Figures S1–S2 for screening.

key_findings.claim: AC16 donor-cell engineering produced characterized ZFP36OE-EV and control-EV preparations.
key_findings.context: Lentiviral ZFP36 overexpression versus empty-vector controls; extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization.

evidence.label: Donor cells
evidence.value: Stable ZFP36-overexpressing AC16 cells; producer-cell qPCR and immunoblot confirmation, n = 3 in Figure 2A-C.

evidence.label: EV preparation
evidence.value: Conditioned medium was collected after 24 hours in EV-depleted serum medium. The EV preparation used sequential clearing, filtration and washing by ultracentrifugation at 120,000 × g.

evidence.label: Characterization
evidence.value: Nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) measured particle size and distribution. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed vesicular morphology. The immunoblots detected CD9, CD63 and TSG101. The negative marker calnexin was undetected.

evidence.label: Size comparison
evidence.value: Figure 2E labels the mean particle-size comparison nonsignificant, n = 3.

evidence.label: Biological unit
evidence.value: ZFP36OE-EV names the preparation released by engineered donor cells; donor expression is distinct from a quantified ZFP36 cargo dose in recipient cells.

evidence.label: Preparation variability reported in main text
evidence.value: Results §3.2 states that Supplementary Results §3 gives yields and protein-to-particle ratios for three independent EV preparations. The individual values remain unresolved.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF p. 2, Methods §§2.3–2.4, p. 5, Figure 2A–G and caption, and p. 9, Results §3.2. Results cites Supplementary Results §3 for preparation yields and ratios.

key_findings.claim: Engineered EVs improved endothelial viability and ferroptosis-related readouts under RSL3 exposure.
key_findings.context: HUVEC free-EV experiment comparing engineered EVs with empty-vector donor-cell EVs under the same chemical stress.

evidence.label: Exposure and dose
evidence.value: 0.5 µM RSL3 for 12 hours. EVs were added with RSL3 at 3,000 NTA-counted particles per seeded cell.

evidence.label: Main comparison
evidence.value: Untreated HUVECs, RSL3 alone, Ctrl-EV + RSL3 and ZFP36OE-EV + RSL3.

evidence.label: Observed directions
evidence.value: Engineered-EV treatment had higher CCK-8 viability, lower DCFH-DA ROS and C11-BODIPY oxidation, greater JC-1 aggregate/monomer ratio, lower COX-2 and higher GPX4 than control EVs under stress.

evidence.label: Assay scales
evidence.value: Figure 3A CCK-8 n = 5; quantified ROS, JC-1, immunoblot and C11-BODIPY panels n = 3.

evidence.label: Pharmacological control
evidence.value: Ferrostatin-1 (1 µM, given one hour before RSL3) is the pharmacological control for the C11-BODIPY measurement in Figure 3I–J.

evidence.label: Label signal reported in main text
evidence.value: Results §3.3 reports PKH26 fluorescence associated with HUVECs after six hours with either labelled EV preparation. Figure S3 and its underlying images remain uninspected. The reported label signal does not quantify intact EV internalization or cargo transfer.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF pp. 2–3, Methods §§2.5 and 2.7, p. 6, Figure 3A–J and caption, and p. 9, Results §3.3. The Results text cites Figure S3 for PKH26 fluorescence.

key_findings.claim: Intramyocardial engineered-EV delivery improved day-21 cardiac readouts in the mouse MI experiment.
key_findings.context: A direct myocardial-injection study, separate from the NiTi coating and rat arterial implantation experiments.

evidence.label: Groups and delivery
evidence.value: MI + PBS, MI + Ctrl-EV and MI + ZFP36OE-EV. During surgery, each EV-treated mouse received a total of 20 µg EV protein in 20 µL across five infarct-border-zone sites.

evidence.label: Cardiac function
evidence.value: Figure 4C and E show higher left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening with engineered EVs than with control EVs on day 21 (n = 6). Baseline comparisons in Figure 4B and D are labelled nonsignificant.

evidence.label: Tissue endpoint
evidence.value: Figure 4F–G shows myocardial histology and a smaller Sirius Red fibrosis area with engineered EVs than with control EVs (n = 5 for area quantification).

evidence.label: Interpretive unit
evidence.value: These functional and histological results concern directly injected EV preparations in infarcted mice.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF p. 3, Methods §2.6, p. 7, Figure 4A–G and caption, and pp. 9 and 11, Results §3.4.

key_findings.claim: PDA/HA modification enabled EV immobilization and gradual particle release from NiTi surfaces.
key_findings.context: Material characterization and an in-vitro PBS release experiment on engineered-EV-functionalized NiTi.

evidence.label: Material sequence
evidence.value: Bare NiTi was modified with polydopamine (PDA) to make N-P, followed by hyaluronic acid (HA) to make NPH, then functionalized with engineered EVs to make NPH@Z-EV. Figure 5A–F shows increased surface roughness and decreasing contact angle after successive modifications, alongside microscopy and PKH26-associated surface fluorescence.

evidence.label: EV immobilization
evidence.value: NPH was incubated with EV suspension at 25 µg/mL for 12 hours at 4 °C, followed by three gentle PBS washes.

evidence.label: Loading estimate
evidence.value: 72.80% ± 0.83% (mean ± SD, n = 3). The estimate subtracts particles recovered from unbound suspension and washes from the input particle count and divides that difference by the input count.

evidence.label: Release
evidence.value: EV-associated particles were detected by NTA during 14 days in PBS at 37 °C (n = 3). Cumulative release is expressed relative to the estimated initial number of immobilized particles.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF p. 3, Methods §§2.8–2.9, p. 8, Figure 5A–I, p. 9, Figure 5 caption, and p. 11, Results §3.5.

key_findings.claim: Engineered-EV coatings protected directly contacting endothelial cells under ferroptosis-related stress.
key_findings.context: Direct HUVEC-material contact with a control-EV coating comparator.

evidence.label: Experimental groups
evidence.value: NiTi, NiTi + RSL3, NPH + RSL3, NPH@Ctrl-EV + RSL3 and NPH@Z-EV + RSL3.

evidence.label: Conditions
evidence.value: Cells were seeded directly onto the substrate and exposed to 0.5 µM RSL3 for 12 hours where indicated.

evidence.label: Observed directions
evidence.value: NPH@Z-EV yielded a higher live-cell percentage and lower C11-BODIPY oxidized/reduced fluorescence ratio than NPH@Ctrl-EV under stress; quantified panels n = 3.

evidence.label: Additional source-reported arm
evidence.value: Results §3.5 reports higher viability, lower reactive oxygen species, better preservation of mitochondrial membrane potential, partial GPX4 restoration and lower COX-2 with engineered-EV coating extracts than with NPH extracts under stress. These are main-text reports linked to Figure S4. The extract plots and numerical values remain uninspected.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF p. 3, Methods §2.10, p. 8, Figure 5J–M, p. 9, Figure 5 caption, and p. 11, Results §3.5. Results cites Figure S4 for the separate coating-extract assays.

key_findings.claim: The engineered coating improved vascular-repair-associated markers in a day-14 rat arterial implant model.
key_findings.context: Femoral-artery injury with intraluminal NiTi filaments in male Sprague-Dawley rats.

evidence.label: Actual implant comparison
evidence.value: The three groups were bare NiTi, PDA/HA-modified NPH and engineered-EV-coated NPH@Z-EV. Arteries were collected at day 14. The control-EV coating was tested in the separate cell-contact experiment.

evidence.label: Histology and marker directions
evidence.value: The NPH@Z-EV group showed better-preserved architecture and less neointimal thickening and inflammatory infiltration. Its staining measurements show higher CD31 and α-SMA positive areas and lower TNF-α, OPN and 4-HNE positive areas relative to bare NiTi and PDA/HA-modified NPH.

evidence.label: Quantitative panel scales
evidence.value: Figure 6C–F and H captions give n = 5 for quantitative staining. These measurements are markers of endothelial recovery, inflammation, smooth-muscle-associated remodeling and lipid oxidation.

evidence.label: Source-reported cytokine support
evidence.value: Results §3.6 reports lower serum IL-1β in the NPH@Z-EV group and no significant difference in IL-10 across groups. Figure S5 and its supporting values remain uninspected.

evidence.label: Use in discussion
evidence.value: Together these endpoints support a short-term vascular-interface repair response and comparison of material controls, endothelial recovery, smooth-muscle-associated remodeling and local lipid oxidation.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF pp. 2–4, Methods §§2.1 and 2.11, p. 10, Figure 6A–H, and pp. 11–12, Figure 6 caption and Results §3.6. Results cites Figure S5 for serum cytokines.

what_this_adds: Tests donor-cell-engineered EVs across endothelial stress, direct myocardial delivery and a functionalized implant interface.
Provides a concrete PDA/HA-NiTi immobilization sequence with particle-based loading/release and directly contacting endothelial assays.
Pairs short-term arterial histology with endothelial, inflammation, smooth-muscle-associated and lipid-oxidation tissue markers, with the actual comparator arms explicit.

supports: The observed preclinical EV-preparation and endothelial-intervention comparisons.
Day-21 mouse function/fibrosis after myocardial injection and day-14 rat arterial tissue-marker responses to the coated filament.
Particle/material characterization and direct-contact coating comparisons under the reported laboratory conditions.
does_not_establish: An isolated ZFP36-cargo causal mechanism or long-term in-vivo EV retention/release and implant durability.
An in-vivo engineered-versus-control-EV coating comparison: that arm appears in the cell contact experiment, not the rat implant experiment.
Clinical coronary stent effectiveness, human treatment benefit or comprehensive chronic biosafety.

qa.question: What was engineered, and what does ZFP36OE-EV mean?
qa.answer: AC16 donor cells were engineered to overexpress ZFP36. Their released EV preparation is called ZFP36OE-EV. Empty-vector-transduced AC16 cells supplied control EVs. Figure 2 shows donor-cell expression and EV particle size, morphology and marker characterization.

qa.question: What endothelial injury conditions and EV dose were tested?
qa.answer: The HUVEC experiment used 0.5 µM RSL3 for 12 hours and 3,000 NTA-counted EV particles per seeded cell. Engineered EVs improved viability and mitochondrial membrane-potential readouts and reduced reactive oxygen species and lipid oxidation relative to control EVs. Ferrostatin-1 served as a control specifically in the C11-BODIPY lipid-oxidation assay.

qa.question: What mouse cardiac result followed direct EV injection?
qa.answer: During MI surgery, each EV-treated mouse received a total of 20 µg EV protein in 20 µL across five infarct-border-zone sites. Compared with control EVs, engineered EVs gave higher left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening at day 21 (n = 6) and lower fibrosis area (n = 5).

qa.question: How were EVs incorporated into NiTi and what release was measured?
qa.answer: Polydopamine followed by hyaluronic acid produced the NPH surface, which was incubated with engineered EVs and washed. Particle loading was 72.80% ± 0.83% (mean ± SD, n = 3). Nanoparticle tracking analysis measured EV-associated particles released over 14 days into PBS at 37 °C.

qa.question: Did the cell-material experiment include a control-EV coating?
qa.answer: Yes. The stressed HUVECs contacted bare NiTi, NPH, NPH with control EVs or NPH with engineered EVs. Bare NiTi without RSL3 served as the baseline. The engineered coating gave a higher live-cell percentage and lower C11-BODIPY oxidation than the control-EV coating (n = 3 for the quantified assays).

qa.question: What did the rat arterial implant experiment show?
qa.answer: At day 14, arteries with engineered-EV-coated filaments showed better-preserved architecture, higher CD31 and α-SMA positive areas, and lower TNF-α, OPN and 4-HNE positive areas than bare NiTi and PDA/HA-modified NPH (n = 5 for the marker panels). The rat experiment used those three material groups. Control-EV coating was tested in the separate cell-contact experiment.

qa.question: What does the main paper report about the supplementary analyses?
qa.answer: The main article reports transcriptomic screening and Figure 1 shows day-3 mouse expression results. Main Results describes the mismatch in GABARAPL1 between the human screen and mouse comparison. It also reports EV preparation variability, HUVEC-associated fluorescent label, coating-extract effects and serum cytokines. The cited plots in Figures S1–S5 and the preparation yields and protein-to-particle ratios remain unresolved.

qa.question: Which comparisons are most useful for designing follow-up studies?
qa.answer: The study separates particle-dose treatment of stressed cells, protein-dose myocardial injection and material-interface delivery. It uses control EVs in the free-EV, myocardial-injection and direct-contact experiments. The rat filament experiment uses bare NiTi and PDA/HA-modified NPH controls. These designs support comparisons of delivery routes, material controls and assay units.

limitations: Engineering AC16 cells alters a complete EV preparation; the responsible cargo and downstream molecular pathway remain unresolved.
The rat implant study has no control-EV coating arm. Mouse myocardial injection and rat vascular implantation support different delivery-specific endpoints.
The release study measures particles in PBS over 14 days. Longer-term coating stability, intact-cargo delivery, reproduction using primary-cell EVs and chronic biosafety remain open.

The main article describes supplementary screens and assays. Exact discovery cohort identities, preparation yields and protein-to-particle ratios, and detailed values from Figures S3–S5 remain unresolved.

related_papers.relationship: A separate preclinical cardiac-delivery study tests peptide-functionalized miR-185-5p-inhibitor liposomes in DOX-associated cellular and mouse injury. It provides a companion example of carrier characterization, cardiac delivery and cell-injury readout selection with a different formulation and injury model.

provenance.version_of_record: Colloids and Surfaces B: Biointerfaces, volume 270 (2027), article 116261. Published online 15 October 2026.
provenance.evidence_basis: Original article, Methods §§2.1–2.12, Results §§3.1–3.6 and Figures 1–6.
provenance.source_note_supplements: Appendix A points to the publication DOI for supplementary data. The main text describes the S1–S2 screen, preparation yields and ratios, Figure S3 PKH26 fluorescence, Figure S4 coating extracts and Figure S5 serum cytokines. The supplementary figures and exact numeric values remain unresolved.
provenance.source_note_units: Free-EV treatment uses NTA-counted particles per seeded cell. Myocardial injection uses EV protein mass. Coating loading and release are based on NTA particle counts. The reported sample sizes are assay-specific.
provenance.source_note_controls: Control EVs are included in the free-EV endothelial, myocardial injection and direct-contact coating experiments. The rat groups are bare NiTi, PDA/HA-modified NPH and engineered-EV-coated NPH@Z-EV.
provenance.source_note_statistics: Methods §2.12 reports two-sided Student’s t tests and one-way ANOVA, followed by LSD or Tamhane’s T2 post hoc tests as appropriate. The Figure 6 caption prints P < 0.01 for both the two-star and three-star annotations.
